alignments.note: Supplied subordinator for a clause with no conjunction morpheme in it, `added` under rule 55; counting the clause's conjunctions against the ASV's subordinators leaves this one unlicensed.

Noun with the determiner the ASV supplies under rule 15. The copula *be* is not this unit's: rule 20 sends the construction-supplied copula to the predicate, and a predicate morpheme is present in `בְּלֹא־דַעַת`, so the explicit subject takes only its own English.

Preposition plus negative rendered by the single word *without*; rule 30's one-rendering condition is met and the unit heads on the negation, as rule 48 heads `מֵאֵין`. The clause's supplied *be* is the copula of this prepositional predicate and joins the unit under rules 20 and 49, which rule 30 says does not defeat the condition (`לִפְנֵי` → *was before*). The competing reading puts *be* on the subject `נֶפֶשׁ`; rule 20's sentence that an explicit subject takes only its own English where a predicate morpheme stands is why I did not take it.
Predicate adjective of the main clause with its construction-supplied copula, discontinuous around the negative under rule 25.
Anarthrous participle with rule 46's supplied *he that*; head on the word carrying the lexeme under rule 31.
Supplied possessive with no suffix or other possessive morpheme in the phrase, `added` under rule 18's closing sentence.
Participial predicate to *sinneth*; the margin's *misseth his way* was read and set aside under rule 38.

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment gave the subordinate clause's copula *be* to the subject `נֶפֶשׁ`, but rule 20 sends a construction-supplied copula to the predicate wherever a predicate morpheme stands, and rule 49 puts it on the preposition heading a prepositional predicate. *be* now joins the `בְּ`+`לֹא` unit rendered *without*.
Both marginal notes were read and set aside; the printed text governs under rule 38.
